title: When the Smile Wakes
premise: Odile Ashgrove hosts the graveyard-shift call-in show 'Nightline' in the decaying town of Vesper Hollow, where last week's dead keep phoning in with calm, reasonable requests. When an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside beneath the old Ashgrove foundry, Odile learns his family were the town's founders—and its jailers—bound by a ritual that must be renewed every hundred years or whatever they locked away walks free wearing borrowed faces. As the dead callers grow more insistent and the people he loves begin smiling wrong, Odile must choose between completing the ritual (which demands a living heir's heart) and breaking it (which may unmake everyone the founders ever saved). He ends it by giving the door what no Ashgrove ever offered: an apology spoken aloud, opening it willingly—freeing the thing inside not as a prisoner but as a grieving twin, at the cost of his own name and voice.
about_author: Marguerite Delacroix is the pen name of a former late-night radio producer who spent seven years answering calls she suspected were not entirely of this world. She writes in unlit rooms and insists her novels are transcriptions, not inventions.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: POV Odile. On the night shift, Odile takes a call from Mrs. Pell, who died Tuesday; her voice is warm, staticky, and asks him to water her ferns. He complies without telling anyone. The beat is quiet dread: routine horror worn smooth into habit, establishing Odile's loneliness and his talent for keeping doors counted and lights on.

chapters.title: The Excavation
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Crews tearing up the foundry lot for a condo development hit something that isn't foundation: a door, iron-banded, sealed from the inside with wax and hair. The foreman smiles too widely when he describes it. Odile feels the town's attention pivot toward him like a lens focusing. Beat: intrusion—the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Counted
chapters.summary: POV Odile, with flashback fragments. In the Ashgrove house he finds ledgers: names, dates, and tallies in his grandmother's hand—every sealed door, every renewal, every 'offering.' The last entry is dated next month. Beat: inheritance revealed as obligation; Odile realizes his invisibility was arranged, not accidental.

chapters.title: Callers
chapters.summary: POV Odile on air. The dead callers stop making requests and start giving instructions: count the hinges, don't let them open it before the dark of the moon, 'she only wants to be recognized.' A living caller—a city archivist named Wren—phones asking about the foundry, and her voice cuts through the static like daylight. Beat: fragile connection against encroaching duty.

chapters.title: The Smiling Man
chapters.summary: POV alternating Odile/Wren. People around town begin smiling identically—the foreman, the diner cook, Odile's neighbor. Wren arrives with founding-era photographs showing an Ashgrove twin erased from every record. Something wearing that smile visits the station after sign-off. Beat: identity erodes; love interest enters the danger zone.

chapters.title: Renewal
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The ledger's final page details the ritual: a founder's blood, a founder's voice, a founder's heart—given freely before the moon turns. The dead callers beg him to run. His mother's ghost (or memory) appears and admits she kept him small so the door would never find him worthy. Beat: betrayal and clarity; duty fully priced.

chapters.title: Wren, Interrupted
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Researching in the county archive, Wren finds the truth: the sealed thing is Aurelia Ashgrove, the forgotten twin, walled in alive in 1924 to anchor a bargain that keeps Vesper Hollow prosperous and plague-free. She races to warn Odile as the smiling townsfolk converge. Beat: love against duty made literal—she chooses him over the town's secret safety.

chapters.title: The Dark of the Moon
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The door unseals itself a crack; the smiling ones gather in the foundry dark, patient and polite. Odile begins the ritual as instructed—knife, ledger, incantation—but hears Aurelia's true voice beneath the static: not hunger, but a century of being unheard. Beat: climax threshold; he lowers the knife.

chapters.title: Open
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Instead of the offering, Odile opens the door from the outside and speaks the apology no founder ever gave, naming Aurelia aloud. The dead callers sing one note. The smiling ones collapse into ordinary exhausted people. Aurelia steps out—not free of grief, but free of the wall. Beat: climax resolved through recognition rather than sacrifice.

chapters.title: Sign-Off
chapters.summary: POV Wren, then Odile. The price: Odile's name and voice are absorbed into the closing seal—he can host no more shows, and records of 'Odile Ashgrove' fade. But Wren remembers, and says his name nightly until it takes root again. Final scene: a new voice reads the sign-off; somewhere, a fern thrives. Beat: bittersweet resolution—identity surrendered, then rebuilt through love.
